messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The cracks are showing—more than just the usual cracks. The regime’s still holding, but the way people are talking now isn’t just frustration anymore; it’s like they’re already rehearsing what comes next. And the fact that even the *newspapers* are eating their own words? That’s not just sloppiness—that’s the first real sign they’re losing their grip on the narrative. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The moment’s coming, but we need to know *when* before we know *how*."*"
Sender 2: "*"The cracks are showing—cabinet shuffles reversed, budgets hidden, even my landlord (of all people) hinting at exits. The regime’s still standing, but the pieces are wobbling, and the street’s starting to whisper louder than the sermons. Stay sharp—this could tip fast, or drag on just as dangerous."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, it’s not over—but it’s not breaking either. The regime’s holding together by sheer inertia, but the cracks are there, and people are starting to test them quietly. The real question isn’t whether they’ll fall tomorrow, but whether the opposition can outlast their own exhaustion. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this is the calm before something, not the end of it."*"
Sender 4: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping—we can all feel it. The leaks, the bots tripping over themselves, the money moving quietly while the streets stay calm… they’re not in control anymore, just buying time. The question isn’t *if* things break, but how fast—and whether we’re ready when they do."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the regime’s still standing—but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation. The walls are up, the lights are on, but the money’s running out, the soldiers are restless, and people are finally talking again. If something doesn’t give soon, it’ll either collapse or lash out hard. Either way, we should be ready."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’re holding things together for now, but the cracks are showing—elites are hedging their bets, the security forces are hiding something, and the streets are patchy, like a storm waiting to pick a direction. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but what pushes it over the edge first."*"
Sender 7: "*"Something’s shifting—elite cracks, security turning on itself, even the tea house is buzzing with purpose instead of just complaints. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a dam with too many leaks—no one knows which one will break first, but the water’s rising."*"
Sender 8: "*"The regime’s still in control, but it’s like watching a house of cards—everyone’s holding their breath to see which way it’ll fall. The fear’s still there, but people are starting to whisper, and that’s the dangerous part. Stay sharp, keep your plans quiet, and don’t trust the calm."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, the regime’s not panicking—that’s the real takeaway. They’re tightening the inner circle, loosening the grip on the streets, and even the neighbors are treating them like they’ll be around for a while. People are talking more, but no one’s moving yet. It’s like watching a storm from a distance—you can see the clouds, but the wind hasn’t hit us. Yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"Something’s stuck—no one’s in a hurry to move, but no one’s willing to break the silence either. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding slower, and the people who should be in charge are all looking over their shoulders instead of giving orders. Keep your eyes open, but don’t make any sudden moves—this isn’t over, but it’s not collapsing yet either."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are still standing, but the cracks are there—just not where you’d expect. The bosses are playing their usual games, the kids are chanting like it’s a drill, and the internet’s crawling because someone’s nervous, but the real tell? The census got ‘postponed’ while they’re breaking ground on new palaces. They’re betting on time, not change—but time’s the one thing no one’s got a handle on."*"
Sender 12: "*"The regime’s grip is slipping, but not fast enough for them to panic—yet. The real question is whether they’ll try to tighten their hold or cut their losses before the cracks turn into a collapse. Either way, the air feels different now—people are talking like they’ve got nothing left to lose."*"
Sender 13: "*"Something’s breaking—quietly, but fast. The elites aren’t talking to each other, the security forces are dragging their feet, and even the pharmacist is stocking up like he’s expecting a storm. The regime’s still barking orders, but it’s all for show—no one’s listening anymore. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. This could be the moment we’ve been waiting for."*"
Sender 14: "*"Something’s shifting—you can feel it in the air. The walls are cracking, but no one’s sure if it’s just a tremor or the whole thing coming down. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and watch for who’s suddenly talking to who."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, the machine is still running smoothly—too smoothly, honestly. The checkpoints are down, the shops are full, and even the hospitals aren’t seeing the usual panic. But that’s exactly what worries me. They’re not just holding on; they’re *ahead*—like they already know what we’re thinking before we do. For now, we’re in the eye of the storm. But storms don’t stay still."*"
Sender 16: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure if it’ll hold or collapse under the next storm. The fear’s still there, but people are starting to whisper that staying quiet might be the real danger now."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the rumors about cracks are just noise—they’re still playing the long game, not scrambling. The real tell? The taxi drivers are betting on change, but the regime’s acting like they’ve got time. That’s either arrogance or they’ve got something we’re not seeing yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The cracks are showing—cabinet’s moving like a machine, but the streets are humming with something else. My neighbor’s got a bag packed, airlines are adding flights, and even the censors are slipping. Not a collapse yet, but the regime’s holding its breath too—just not sure for how long."*"
Sender 19: "*"They’re holding on, but it’s getting harder—you can feel it in the cracks. The fear’s still there, but now the real danger is staying quiet. Watch the construction sites and the civil servants; they’re telling us more than the speeches."*"
Sender 20: "*"The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a building with cracks in the foundation—no one’s sure when (or if) it’ll collapse, but the foundation’s definitely shifting. People are starting to whisper ‘what if’ a little louder, but no one’s ready to bet their life on it yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there—security forces are dragging their feet, the money’s shaky, and the censors are scrambling to keep up. The question isn’t if things will break, but whether the pieces fall fast or slow—so let’s stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready to move when the moment comes."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the machine is still humming—no stuttering, no panic. The real tension isn’t out in the open; it’s in the cracks: security turning on itself, banks tightening the screws *just* enough to notice, and the young ones talking louder because they think no one’s listening. The regime’s not cracking—it’s tightening. But the question isn’t if, it’s when the squeeze becomes too much. Stay sharp, and keep your exits quiet."*"
Sender 23: "*"Listen—this isn’t just cracks in the walls anymore. The whole thing is coming down, and they’re not even trying to hide it. The doctors, the lawyers, even the security forces—they’re all moving in the same direction, and the only question left is whether it collapses fast or slow. Stay sharp, but don’t panic. We’re past the point of no return."*"
Sender 24: "*"Listen—things are *shifting*, but no one’s sure which way yet. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like watching a house of cards where half the cards are missing—one wrong move, and it all comes down. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and be ready to move fast if things tip."*"
Sender 25: "*"Something’s off—elites aren’t talking to each other, the budget’s missing, and even my neighbor’s got an escape plan. The regime’s still holding, but the cracks are showing, and they’re starting to *feel* it too. Stay sharp."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
